item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-15
item.description: On 2026-11-14 two institutions published their account of the same thing, and the accounts do not describe the same object. In Shanghai, the 2026 Industrial Operating System Conference (12-13 November) formally opened the establishment of an Industrial Operating System Standards Working Group under MIIT's Industrial Software Standardization Technical Committee, released a CCID research report on the technology and industry, and launched a 'pilot validation formation' for steel, non-ferrous mining, rail transit and nuclear power. The instruments named are a reference architecture, interconnection, compatibility and test evaluation -- every one of them a procurement instrument. On the same day in Hangzhou the eleventh COSCon opened at Yun Valley, co-hosted by KAIYUANSHE -- a volunteer community with no registered legal entity -- and Datawhale, under the guidance of a municipal AI-open-source college and with the backing of a Hangzhou Open Source AI Foundation, the West Lake district talent office and a provincial AI academy. It published the first China AI Open Source Ecosystem Blue Book, handed out the first batch of 'open source mentor' credentials, and named six 'typical cities'. One announcement governs a production floor and no source code; the other celebrates a commons and names no maintainer. The distance between them is the day's finding, and six weeks of this series has been circling it from every instrument angle available.
